items.title: Jimmy Owens interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I’m looking at your, the mid-60s, early, mid-60s, really a lot of different, great names here that you were with: Maynard Ferguson and Gerry Mulligan and Charles Mingus. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. I worked with Mulligan...

ctx.x: I went on from there to play with all of the masters of the music, and that’s where I really feel very, very privileged, and like I said, other than at Lincoln Center, I mean that Lincoln Hospital job in the Bronx, I’ve never worked outside of music in all of my years.
I’m looking at your, the mid-60s, early, mid-60s, really a lot of different, great names here that you were with: Maynard Ferguson and Gerry Mulligan and Charles Mingus.

Yeah. I worked with Mulligan for a shorter period of time. I worked at Birdland with him for I think it was a one week engagement. And I did a few concerts. This was when he had the concert jazz band, which was a precursor to the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band. Thad was in this band, Mel Lewis played drums in the band, and it was from that experience that Mel Lewis and Thad — well I knew Thad, I’d met Thad some years before — invited me to be in the Thad Jones and Mel Lewis Jazz Orchestra. But I mean my work with…

items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: They worked with people like Slide Hampton, Maynard Ferguson, Woody Herman, you know?

ctx.x: Okay. So, I’m sorry, but could you talk about the Newport Youth Band?

So, in the Newport Youth Band there are a number of musicians who became professional musicians. There were three trumpet players, you know, this is besides myself, and trombonists. They worked with people like Slide Hampton, Maynard Ferguson, Woody Herman, you know? The pianist is someone who writes lots of music, Michael Benny. The drummer was Larry Rosen, who started GRP records. Him and his partner Dave Grusin built that record company up and then sold it for 40 million dollars.

It was just the two of them! So, the education that we got at the Newport Youth Band was very, very important. The bass player, Eddie Gomez, is around. Of the people who are around now, it’s just Eddie Gomez, baritone saxophonist Ronnie Cuber, and myself, and Michael Benny. That’s it.
